items.title: Section: Sixteen Aspects Sorted Into Three Gates of Liberation — Emptiness, Wishlessness, and Signlessness

items.zh: 復次，此十六行，幾是空行？謂二，即苦諦後二行。幾是無願行？謂六，即苦諦前二行及集諦一切。幾是無相行？謂滅諦一切。幾是清淨因所顯行？謂道諦一切。問：要由無常想，能住無我想，何故此中先說空耶？答：此約無我觀已生，由無常觀建立無願；以此二觀，前後展轉互修治故。
items.en: Of these sixteen aspects, how many belong to emptiness? Two — the truth of suffering's last two. How many to wishlessness? Six — the truth of suffering's first two, and the entirety of the truth of origin. How many to signlessness? The entirety of the truth of cessation. How many are aspects revealed by the cause of purification? The entirety of the truth of the path. Question: since impermanence must precede selflessness, why is emptiness named first here? Answer: this describes the sequence only after selflessness's own insight has already arisen, wishlessness being established through the contemplation of impermanence; the two contemplations reinforce one another repeatedly, not in a single fixed order.

items.title: Section: Illness, Its Cause, Its Cure, and the Medicine — Why Suffering Is Named First

items.zh: 復次，四聖諦說次第者，謂由此故苦，此最為初；如此故苦，此為第二；此二攝黑品究竟。由此故樂，此為第三；如此故樂，是為第四；此二攝白品究竟。譬如重病、病因、病愈、良藥。又有差別。謂如世間遭苦次第，當知建立聖諦次第。
items.en: Furthermore, as for the sequence in which the four noble truths are taught: because of this, there is suffering — this comes first; suffering being so, this is second — these two exhaust the dark side. Because of this, there is peace — this is third; peace being so, this is fourth — these two exhaust the bright side. It is like a serious illness, its cause, its cure, and the medicine that brings the cure about. There is also a further explanation: the sequence in which noble truths are established follows the very sequence in which ordinary beings encounter suffering in the world.

items.zh: 所以者何？如諸世間曾所遭苦，即於此處先發作意；次於遭苦因，次於苦解脫，後於解脫方便，發起作意。

items.title: Section: What "Truth" Actually Means — And Why the Four Noble Truths Belong to the Ultimate

items.zh: 問：諦義云何？答：如所說相不捨離義，由觀此故到清淨究竟義，是諦義。問：苦諦義云何？答：煩惱所生行義。問：集諦義云何？答：能生苦諦義。問：滅諦義云何？答：彼俱寂靜義。問：道諦義云何？答：能成三諦義。問：如是四聖諦，為世俗諦攝，為勝義諦攝？答：勝義諦攝。何以故？於順苦、樂、不苦不樂諸行中，由自相差別故，建立世俗諦。
items.en: Question: what is the meaning of truth? Answer: the inseparability of a thing from its accepted description; and the ultimate, pure realisation arrived at through direct observation — both are the meaning of truth. Question: what is the meaning of the truth of suffering? Answer: what affliction generates and where it operates. Origin? What generates suffering. Cessation? The mutual stilling of both. The path? What accomplishes all three. Question: do the four noble truths belong to conventional or ultimate truth? Answer: to the ultimate. Why? Because conventional truth is established through discriminating self-characteristics among ordinary experiences of pleasure, pain, and neutrality.

items.title: Section: One Shared Taste of Suffering — Why Only the Noble Ones Can Actually See It

items.zh: 由彼共相一味苦故，當知建立勝義諦。
items.en: Because these phenomena share a single common characteristic, a single taste of suffering, one should know that ultimate truth is established on this basis.

items.title: Section: Why Suffering Must Be Known First — And Cultivating the Path Comes Last

items.zh: 問：何緣故說遍知苦諦、永斷集諦、觸證滅諦、修習道諦？答：由彼苦諦是四顛倒所依處故，為除顛倒，故遍知苦。既遍知苦，即遍知集，由彼集諦苦諦攝故。雖遍知苦，仍為集諦之所隨逐，故須更說永斷集諦。言觸證者，是現見義。由於滅諦現前見故，不生怖畏，愛樂攝受，是故次說觸證滅諦。若勤修道，乃能成辦所說三義，是故後說修習道諦。
items.en: Question: why is it said one thoroughly knows suffering, permanently severs origin, directly realises cessation, and cultivates the path? Answer: because suffering is the very ground of the four inverted views, thoroughly knowing it is needed to remove them; thoroughly knowing suffering already includes knowing origin, since origin is subsumed under suffering. Yet since origin's own latent seed still follows even after this, its permanent severing must be separately taught. "Realisation" means direct perception; once cessation is directly perceived, no fear arises, only delight in embracing it, hence realisation is named next. Only through diligent cultivation of the path can all three of these be accomplished, hence cultivation is named last.

items.title: Section: Six Kinds of Direct Realisation — Beginning With Settled Thought, Unshakeable Faith, and Precepts Naturally Kept

items.zh: 問：諦現觀有幾種？此復何相？答：決定義是現觀義。此則於諸諦中決定智慧及彼因、彼相應、彼共有法為體，是名現觀相。此復六種應知，如有尋有伺地說。此中云何名初現觀？謂於諸諦決定思惟。云何名為第二現觀？謂三寶所三種淨信，由於寶義已決定故，及聞所成決定智慧。云何名為第三現觀？謂聖所愛戒，於惡趣業已得決定不作律儀故。
items.en: Question: how many kinds of direct realisation of the truths are there, and what characterises them? Answer: decisive certainty is the meaning of realisation — a settled wisdom regarding the truths, together with its cause, accompanying factors, and shared basis, constitute realisation's own character. This is of six kinds. What is the first? Settled reflection upon the truths. What is the second? Threefold pure confidence towards the Three Jewels, their value having been settled, together with the settled wisdom formed through hearing. What is the third? The precepts cherished by the noble ones, one's own settled determination never to commit deeds leading to the lower realms.

items.zh: 云何名為第四現觀？謂於加行道中，先集資糧極圓滿故，又善方便磨瑩心故，從世間順決擇分邊際善根無間，有初內遣有情假法緣心生，能除軟品見道所斷煩惱麁重。

items.title: Section: Three Moments of the True Path of Seeing — Releasing the Person, Releasing the Phenomena, Releasing Both at Once

items.zh: 從此無間，第二內遣諸法假法緣心生，能除中品見道所斷煩惱麁重。從此無間，第三遍遣一切有情諸法假法緣心生，能除一切見道所斷煩惱麁重。又此現觀即是見道，亦名雙運道。此中雖有毘鉢舍那品三心及奢摩他品三心，然由雙運合立三心，以於一剎那中止觀俱可得故。當知此諸心，唯緣非安立諦境。又前二心，法智相應；第三心，類智相應。又即由此心勢力故，於苦等安立諦中，有第二現觀位清淨無礙苦等智生；當知依此智故，苦集滅道智得成立。即前三心并止觀品，能證見斷煩惱寂滅，能得永滅一切煩惱及所依事出世間道，是名現觀智諦現觀。
items.en: Immediately following, a second mind arises releasing the provisional notion of phenomena, removing the underlying heaviness of medium-grade afflictions severed on the path of seeing. Immediately following that, a third mind arises releasing both provisional notions of beings and phenomena entirely, removing the underlying heaviness of every affliction severed on the path of seeing. This realisation is itself the path of seeing, also called the path of calming and insight in union. One should know these minds take only the truth not established in words as their object. The first two correspond to direct wisdom; the third to inferential wisdom. Through this same mind's own momentum, within the conventionally taught truths, a second stage of pure, unobstructed wisdom regarding suffering and the rest arises; one should know it is on this basis that wisdom regarding suffering, origin, cessation, and the path becomes fully established. These three moments, together with calming and insight in union, realise the quiescence of every affliction severed by insight, and attain the supramundane path that permanently eliminates all afflictions and their basis — this is called realisation through the wisdom of direct insight.

blocks.text: Why suffering is named first, what makes a "truth" true, and how the noble path of seeing unfolds in three moments of mind.

Two aspects go to emptiness, six to wishlessness, and all of cessation to signlessness. Master Cháng Bǎi: wishlessness is having no defiled longing for a life to come. Before the path of seeing, contemplation of impermanence and suffering comes first, then selflessness and emptiness.

The first two truths exhaust the dark side and the last two the bright, "like a serious illness, its cause, its cure, and the medicine". (Untranslated, 0605b16: just as people in the world who have suffered first attend to the suffering, then its cause, then release, then the means to it.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: what is real in the world is conventional truth; the supramundane real is ultimate truth.

Conventional truth is set by the distinct characteristics of pleasant, painful, and neutral things; ultimate truth by their "one shared taste of suffering". Master Cháng Bǎi: only noble ones see this.
Origin is included in suffering, so knowing suffering includes knowing origin. Master Cháng Bǎi: having known the aggregates as suffering, one knows its cause.
Including threefold pure faith and settled wisdom born of hearing. Decisive certainty is the meaning of realisation.

The three minds of realisation take only suchness beyond words as their object. Master Cháng Bǎi: the first removes the notion of beings; the second removes attachment to phenomena; the third removes both. Calm and insight are united here. (Untranslated, 0605c17: how the fourth realisation arises from the highest worldly roots, removing the softest afflictions cut by seeing.)
"Illness, cause, cure, medicine." The four truths were taught as a doctor's diagnosis, not a philosophy.

quiz.q: How many of the sixteen aspects are of emptiness, wishlessness, and signlessness?
options: emptiness six, suffering's first two and origin; wishlessness two, suffering's last two; signlessness four, cessation
emptiness two, suffering's last two; wishlessness six, suffering's first two and all of origin; signlessness four, cessation
emptiness four, the path; wishlessness four, cessation; signlessness eight, suffering and origin, whose marks must be removed
each gate five and a third
quiz.why: The treatise assigns two aspects to emptiness, six to wishlessness, and all of cessation to signlessness. Master Cháng Bǎi: wishlessness is having no defiled longing for a life to come, which is why impermanence, suffering, and all of origin belong to it.

quiz.q: The English folds 清淨因所顯行 into signlessness: "together with the truth of the path as its revealing cause." What differs?
options: there is no difference: the path's four aspects are signlessness, as the treatise says, and the English merely says so briefly
the Chinese says the path belongs to emptiness
the Chinese says the path is not among the sixteen
it is a separate question: the path's four aspects are aspects revealed by the pure cause, not signlessness; the English merges them and loses a question
quiz.why: The Chinese asks four questions, the last about aspects revealed by the pure cause, answered by all of the path. Master Cháng Bǎi: the four aspects of the path are the causal practice for realising pure cessation. So 2+6+4+4 accounts for all sixteen with four headings. The English reduces this to three, making "signlessness" cover eight aspects.

quiz.q: Since impermanence must precede selflessness, why is emptiness named first here?
options: it speaks after selflessness has arisen; before seeing, impermanence precedes; after realisation one returns to impermanence, the two reinforcing each other
because emptiness matters most, it always comes first, and practice starts with it, with no need for impermanence or suffering first
this is a copyist's error, impermanence belonging first
because only outsiders contemplate impermanence
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: before the path of seeing, in early practice, contemplation of impermanence and suffering arises first, and then that of selflessness and emptiness; after realisation, emerging from non-discriminating wisdom, one goes on with impermanence and suffering in wishlessness. So the two reinforce each other. The English omits "wishlessness established through impermanence."

quiz.q: What simile does the treatise use for the order of the truths, and how are the dark and bright sides divided?
options: king, minister, general, and soldier; suffering and cessation dark, origin and path bright, since suffering and cessation are results
serious illness, its cause, its cure, and medicine; suffering and origin the dark side, cessation and the path the bright
seed, sprout, stem, and fruit; all four truths dark
the four seasons; all four truths bright
quiz.why: The treatise says the first two exhaust the dark side and the last two the bright, like a serious illness, its cause, its cure, and the medicine. Master Cháng Bǎi: suffering is the result and origin the cause, which contain all dark cause and effect; cessation and the path contain all bright cause and effect. The order runs from fruit to cause in each pair.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the two senses of 諦?
options: speech inseparable from a phenomenon's mark is conventional truth; arriving at pure realisation through observation is ultimate truth
whatever can be said is ultimate truth and what cannot is conventional, words being the only way to the real
諦 has one sense only, the written words of scripture
諦 means the laws of the world
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: knowing a phenomenon through conventional speech, with speech inseparable from the mark, belongs to conventional truth; the real in the world is conventional truth, and the supramundane real is ultimate truth. The treatise's definition thus holds both senses in one sentence, which the English divides with "both."

quiz.q: What does the treatise give as the meaning of each of the four truths?
options: suffering, what generates origin; origin, formations born of affliction; cessation, what accomplishes three; the path, the stilling of both
suffering, bodily pain; origin, gathering wealth; cessation, death; the path, a road, all by worldly word sense
suffering, formations born of affliction; origin, what generates suffering; cessation, the stilling of both; the path, what accomplishes all three
all four mean the same, differing only in name
quiz.why: The treatise defines each truth briefly. Master Cháng Bǎi: what affliction generates means birth as a being, and where it operates means the place on which that birth depends; so suffering is the aggregates born of affliction and the place where affliction moves. The English "The mutual stilling of both" adds "mutual," where 俱 only means both.

quiz.q: Why do the four noble truths belong to ultimate truth?
options: conventional truth is set by self-characteristics among phenomena; ultimate truth by their shared taste of suffering
ultimate truth is set by self-characteristics; conventional by the shared taste of suffering, since ordinary beings know suffering too
because the Buddha spoke them himself
because the truths exist only in nirvāṇa
quiz.why: The treatise says that conventional truth is set by the distinct self-characteristics of pleasant, painful, and neutral phenomena, and ultimate truth by their one shared taste of suffering. Master Cháng Bǎi: only noble ones realise this shared mark of all contaminated phenomena; even pleasant and neutral phenomena are impermanent and in the end suffering.

quiz.q: If knowing suffering includes knowing origin, why teach the severing of origin separately?
options: because origin has no relation to suffering, knowing suffering does not include it, and it must be practised separately
because origin is severed only after death
because severing origin is an outsiders' idea to be refuted
though suffering is fully known, one is still followed by origin, so its severing must be taught as well
quiz.why: The treatise reasons that origin is subsumed under suffering, so knowing suffering includes knowing origin; yet one remains followed by origin. Master Cháng Bǎi: having known the aggregates as suffering, one knows suffering is brought by the origin of affliction and karma; still, seeds of these follow one, and origin must be severed to leave suffering.

quiz.q: The English has "Threefold pure confidence towards the Three Jewels, their value having been settled." What is omitted?
options: it omits 及聞所成決定智慧, which the lecture places as contaminated pure faith at the ordinary stage, a second element of this realisation
it mistranslates 三寶: the Chinese has only the Buddha, and "Three Jewels" should be "the Buddha"
it omits nothing: the Chinese has no sense of being settled
it omits precepts, which are the second realisation
quiz.why: The Chinese gives two elements of the second realisation: threefold pure faith, and settled wisdom born of hearing. Master Cháng Bǎi: settled wisdom born of hearing belongs to contaminated pure faith at the ordinary stage. The English stops at the first.

quiz.q: What are the definition and substance of direct realisation?
options: seeing with the eyes is its meaning; eye-consciousness and form are its substance, so it belongs to the five, not mental consciousness
hearing is its meaning; ear-consciousness its substance
decisive certainty is its meaning; settled wisdom regarding the truths, with its cause, accompanying factors, and shared basis, is its substance
accepting on faith is its meaning; faith its substance
quiz.why: The treatise says decisive certainty is the meaning of realisation, and settled wisdom regarding the truths, with its cause, accompanying factors, and shared basis, is its character. Master Cháng Bǎi: unchanging uncontaminated wisdom regarding the four truths is the meaning of realisation. It is thus an insight, not physical sight.

quiz.q: The English has "the unconditioned truth" for 非安立諦. Is this rendering right?
options: yes: 非安立諦 is space and the other unconditioned phenomena, the three minds taking space, so "unconditioned" fits best
no: 非安立諦 is suchness free of verbal marks, not "unconditioned"; "conventionally taught truths" for 安立諦 is apt
no: it should be "conditioned truth"
no: 非安立諦 is conventional truth
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the three minds at realisation take only suchness free of verbal marks as object. 非安立 means not established in words, not unconditioned. The English pair is uneven: "the conventionally taught truths" fits 安立諦, but the corresponding negative would be something like "truth beyond verbal establishment."

quiz.q: What do the second and third minds of seeing remove, and what does the English lack?
options: the first removes phenomena, the second beings, the third nothing; the English has all three without any gap
the first removes the notion of beings, the second of phenomena, the third both; the English starts at the second, wholly lacking the first
all three remove only afflictions, not notions
the three are seeing, cultivation, and beyond learning
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: on entering realisation, the self-mark of the notion of beings is removed, and non-discriminating wisdom joined with the suchness of no-self appears; the second thought removes attachment to phenomena, penetrating that all phenomena are only provisionally named. The third removes both notions. The English begins "a second mind," having lost the first.

quiz.q: Why is this realisation called the path in union, and how do the minds match the two knowledges?
options: each moment has both calm and insight, hence union; the first two minds join dharma-knowledge, the third subsequent knowledge
calm then insight in turn, hence union; the first mind joins dharma-knowledge, the last two subsequent knowledge
body and mind striving together, hence union; all three join dharma-knowledge, with no subsequent knowledge
merit and wisdom together, hence union; all three join subsequent knowledge
quiz.why: The treatise says this realisation is the path of seeing, also the path in union; the first two minds join dharma-knowledge and the third subsequent knowledge. Master Cháng Bǎi: calm and insight are united, and so three minds are spoken of, not six, for each moment has both. Here the treatise holds three moments of true seeing. The English "direct" and "inferential" wisdom are its terms for the two knowledges.
